passage_target: Last April my friend and I took the slow train to the coast instead of the bus. The bus would have taken two hours, but the train took five, and we sat by the window the whole way. passage_target: When our office moved to a smaller building, the team had to decide what to keep. We had stored boxes that nobody had opened for years. My manager, who wanted the new space to feel calm, asked each person to choose one useful item. I found a notebook in which I had written ideas for my first project. We recycled the rest, and the room felt brighter by the end of the day. The change reminded me that old habits can take up space too.

By the time we arrived, the clouds were breaking and the sea was calm. The detour took hours, yet it became the part of the trip we remembered best.

By Monday, the plants had lifted their leaves again. I learned that a small amount of preparation can make a difficult morning easier.

title_target: The Walk That Changed My Routine
passage_target: For months I had been taking a taxi to work, even though the office was only twenty minutes away on foot. A new roadworks project made the traffic slower, so I began walking instead. The route, which follows a canal, is quieter than the main street and passes a bakery that opens early. I used to arrive tense, but now I have time to listen to a podcast before work. I still take a taxi when it rains heavily, although I no longer think of walking as exercise I have to force myself to do.
